issue.title: sase bead create prints and commits the pre-relocation bead ID, so an agent's follow-up commands mutate another agent's bead
issue.description:
REPRODUCED LIVE 2026-08-17 by the sase-o8 land agent. Two agents created a task bead ~30s apart; both locally minted sase-of. The duplicate-ID relocation machinery from closed task sase-f0 worked correctly and moved the losing bead to sase-og, but nothing downstream of the relocation was updated, so the CLI told me my bead was sase-of.

EVIDENCE (shared beads store, sase/repos/beads):
  dd0f91cf 2026-08-17 09:25:16 'chore(beads): create sase-of' -> adds events/streams/sase-of.jsonl  (agent sase-o9.land)
  8c61b3c3 2026-08-17 09:26:00 'chore(beads): create sase-of' -> adds events/streams/sase-og.jsonl  (agent sase-o8.land, MINE)
My commit message still names sase-of while the stream it writes is sase-og. events/streams/sase-og.jsonl event 000001 has issue_id 'sase-og' from its very first event -- so the relocation landed in the stream but never in the caller's view. Stdout read: 'Created task: sase-of - test_derived_only_collision_...'.

CONSEQUENCE (this is the damaging part): I then ran three 'sase bead note sase-of' calls and one 'sase bead update sase-of --status ready' against what the CLI had just told me was my bead. All four hit the OTHER agent's bead. Three long RELATED notes about a test flake were appended to an unrelated Procs-hints-overflow bead, and only the note command's echoed title ('Noted: sase-of - Procs pane hints line overflows...') revealed it. I restored that bead's notes with 'sase bead update --notes' and left a correction note. Nothing was lost -- 'sase bead history' is append-only -- but a less careful agent would not have noticed, and 'sase bead close' or 'update --description' would have been considerably worse than a stray note.

MECHANISM (src/sase/bead/cli_crud_create.py:160-187): proj.create() returns an Issue whose .id is the locally minted ID. The commit message is composed from that stale id at line 182 (require_mutation_commit_message('create', [issue.id])), and line 187 prints it. The relocation happens later, inside the bead_store_mutation sync/conflict path (sase-f0 added merge_bead_event_streams_with_relocation plus the _RelocationIds allocator in conflict_resolver, which already reports 'relocated duplicate beads: <old> -> <new>' into the resolution message and sync log). So the information exists; it just never reaches the Issue object, the commit subject, or stdout.

SCOPE: make the create path report the ID that was actually stored. Candidate approaches for the worker: have the mutation context surface its relocation map and re-resolve issue.id (and the commit subject) before printing; or allocate IDs so a collision cannot happen in the first place; or, at minimum, print a loud 'relocated to <new-id>' line and exit non-zero-ish/warn so an agent scripting against stdout cannot silently address a stranger's bead. Whatever is chosen must also cover the other create surfaces that echo an id (sase bead work / epic phase minting, the ACE Artifacts Beads create action at src/sase/ace/tui/actions/_artifacts_beads_mutations.py:267).

IMPACT: SASE routinely runs many agents concurrently against one shared bead store, and /sase_new_task tells every agent to create-then-note-then-mark-ready. That is exactly the create-then-mutate sequence this defect corrupts. Two beads minted within 45s collided today with only ~6 tasks filed in the preceding hour.

RESIDUAL AFTER sase-f0: sase-f0 fixed the store-wedging half (duplicate issue_created events used to wedge every later sync for ~30 minutes). Relocation is the fix working. This bead is the reporting half that sase-f0 did not cover.

Size medium: the mechanism and the exact lines are identified above; the open decision is which of the three fix shapes to take.
